title: Rectangles to integrals
sub: Riemann sums for ∫₀¹ x² dx, then the area viewed as a function of its right edge.

frames.caption: The area under y = x² from 0 to 1. Approximate it with n rectangles, each as tall as the curve at the left end of its slice.
n = 4: the rectangles add up to 0.21875, off from 1/3 by -0.11458.
n = 8: the rectangles add up to 0.27344, off from 1/3 by -0.05990. Doubling n roughly halves the error.
n = 16: the rectangles add up to 0.30273, off from 1/3 by -0.03060.
n = 32: the rectangles add up to 0.31787, off from 1/3 by -0.01546.
n = 100: the rectangles add up to 0.32835, off from 1/3 by -0.00498.
As n → ∞ every version converges to the same number, 1/3. That limit is the definite integral ∫₀¹ x² dx.
The area under y = x² from 0 to 1. Approximate it with n rectangles, each as tall as the curve at the middle of its slice.
n = 4: the rectangles add up to 0.32812, off from 1/3 by -0.00521.
n = 8: the rectangles add up to 0.33203, off from 1/3 by -0.00130. Doubling n cuts the error by about 4×: midpoints err in both directions and largely cancel.
n = 16: the rectangles add up to 0.33301, off from 1/3 by -0.00033.
n = 32: the rectangles add up to 0.33325, off from 1/3 by -0.00008.
n = 100: the rectangles add up to 0.33332, off from 1/3 by -0.00001.
As n → ∞ every version converges to the same number, 1/3. That limit is the definite integral ∫₀¹ x² dx.
The area under y = x² from 0 to 1. Approximate it with n rectangles, each as tall as the curve at the right end of its slice.
n = 4: the rectangles add up to 0.46875, off from 1/3 by +0.13542.
n = 8: the rectangles add up to 0.39844, off from 1/3 by +0.06510. Doubling n roughly halves the error.
n = 16: the rectangles add up to 0.36523, off from 1/3 by +0.03190.
n = 32: the rectangles add up to 0.34912, off from 1/3 by +0.01579.
n = 100: the rectangles add up to 0.33835, off from 1/3 by +0.00502.
As n → ∞ every version converges to the same number, 1/3. That limit is the definite integral ∫₀¹ x² dx.
Now let the right edge move. A(x) = the area under f(t) = t² from 0 to x. As x slides right, the shaded area grows; record its value as a height (orange).
x = 0.1: area so far 0.000.
x = 0.2: area so far 0.003.
x = 0.3: area so far 0.009.
x = 0.4: area so far 0.021.
Near x = 0.5 the curve is low, so each step right adds only a thin sliver: A grows slowly.
x = 0.6: area so far 0.072.
x = 0.7: area so far 0.114.
x = 0.8: area so far 0.171.
x = 0.9: area so far 0.243.
x = 1.0: area so far 0.333.
x = 1.1: area so far 0.444.
x = 1.2: area so far 0.576.
Near x = 1.3 the curve is tall, so each step adds a thick slice: A climbs steeply.
x = 1.4: area so far 0.915.
x = 1.5: area so far 1.125.

The rate at which the area grows is exactly the height of the curve at the edge: A′(x) = f(x). That is the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. So to find an area, find any function whose derivative is f: here x³/3, which gives ∫₀¹ x² dx = 1/3.
